title.narrative: Consultancy Support to CSO Development in Ukraine, 2019-2024
Konsultstöd till utveckling av civilsamhällesorganisationer i Ukraina, 2019-2024

description.narrative: Ambassaden i Ukraina planerar att fortsätta stödja civilsamhällesorganisationer (CSO:er) för att de ska bli hållbara, ha stark ledning och kapacitet att främja förändringar och reformer i Ukraina. Det tidigare konsultkontraktet har löpt ut, och ambassaden i Kiev skulle vilja upphandla en ny konsult med särskild expertis inom institutionell utveckling av CSO:er.

The Embassy in Ukraine is keen to continue to support civil society organisations (CSOs) to become sustainable, well-managed and capacitated to promote changes and reforms in Ukraine. The previous consultancy contract has expired and the Embassy in Kyiv would like to procure a new consultancy with a special expertise in organizational/institutional development area of CSOs.

Summary of Progress (2019-2024)
Over the course of five years, including two no-cost extensions, the Sida CSO support assignment - implemented by NCG actively engaged more than 15 Ukrainian CSOs in a dynamic, tailored programme of institutional strengthening. The support was underpinned by a dual framework of Results-Based Management (RBM) and Human Rights Based Approaches (HRBA), emphasising strategic planning, transparent governance, stakeholder inclusion, and long-term sustainability.
A total of 14 Systems-Based Audits and six Verification Audits were completed during the assignment, providing baseline data and critical recommendations to guide CSO development. These were followed up with bilateral advisory support, mentoring, action plan implementation, and dedicated training programmes.
Annual and biannual Capacity Development Action plans developed by CSOs and NCG consultants together helped establish shared priorities, internal ownership, institutionalisation and leadership engagement, and a road map for strategic improvement.
Throughout the assignment, over 30 structured learning events were held (always designed as several steps processes with pre- and post-elements and modules), covering topics such as RBM, executive- and board governance, communication strategy, anti-corruption & integrity, conflict sensitivity, environment, gender analysis and mainstreaming, human rights-based approach (HRBA), and EU integration. These learning processes were complemented by tailored technical support - particularly in HR management, audit preparedness, communications, donor reporting, strategy development and financial governance. Starting in December 2021, a few months before the full-scale invasion started, a strong focus emerged on psychological resilience, stress management, and institutional integrity amid war.
The programme was also able to support CSO participation in Sidas strategic priorities, particularly relating to human rights and Ukraines EU integration. The Annual CSO Partner Meetings, resumed post-COVID and war escalation, became critical platforms for knowledge sharing, joint planning, and strategic recalibration. The assignments adaptability - ranging from remote implementation during lockdowns to in-person consultations and partner meetings in Kyiv was central to its success. CSOs supported under this initiative emerged as more coherent, better governed, and more resilient actors within Ukraines democratic and development ecosystem.
3. Activities During July-December 2024 Regular needs assessments conducted by NCG - both during in-person consultations in Kyiv in September, October and December 2024 and through online engagements - helped sustain a responsive and adaptive approach to cooperation with the ten remaining Sida-supported CSO partners during this period. These assessments ensured that capacity development remained timely, relevant, and tailored to the evolving priorities of each organisation. In the second half of 2024 the primary focus of this report - NCGs support centered on consolidating progress made in previous years while addressing the urgent operational and strategic challenges faced by CSOs amid the ongoing war. This final phase of the programme featured a comprehensive mix of trainings, targeted technical assistance, and strategic planning - aimed at preparing partners for their expanding role in Ukraines recovery and EU accession process all of this was explicitly requested by the CSOs;
3.1 Training and Capacity Development Training efforts in the second half of 2024 focused on strengthening internal resilience, enhancing strategic capabilities, and supporting CSO alignment with Ukraines EU integration agenda. Activities were implemented across several key areas:
•Annual CSO Partner Meeting Hlibivka, 34 October 2024 This flagship two-day gathering brought together all Sida-supported CSOs, Sida representatives from Stockholm and the Swedish Embassy, and EU Integration Experts. The Sida Ukraine Strategy (2023-2027) was presented and discussed, and moreover, sessions explored EU integration, wartime public communications, legislative screening cooperation, and organisational resilience. Practical workshops addressed donor engagement, fundraising strategies, and multi-sector collaboration.
•RBM Training for SavED Lviv & Online, November 2024 NCG delivered two bilateral RBM workshops tailored to SavEDs strategic and operational needs. The in-person session in Lviv (89 November) focused on theory of change development, performance indicators, and donor reporting. A follow-up online session supported peer review of results assessment frameworks (RAF) and financial planning tools.
•Training of Trainers (ToT) Psycho-Social Conflict Facilitation for Docudays, 1316 November 2024 This 5-day intensive training equipped moderators documenting war crimes with facilitation tools for high-conflict dialogue, self-care techniques, and trauma-sensitive practices. The course responded directly to the needs expressed by Docudays and others for increased capacity in moderating high-risk interviews.
•Governance and Board-Management Workshop Kyiv, 2021 November 2024 Informed by a governance needs survey, this workshop helped CSOs revisit the division of roles between boards and executive management, fundraising oversight, and decision-making under pressure. Participants included NAM, TIU, CEDEM, IRF, and others.
•Final CSO Reception Kyiv, 3 December 2024 This half-day celebratory event brought together Sida partners to reflect on five years of collaboration. Organised by NCG and hosted in Kyiv, the event featured project highlights, brief addresses from CSOs, and closing remarks by the Swedish Embassy outlining future cooperation pathways.
•Joint CSOGovt Workshop on EU Integration Kyiv, 20 December 2024 Held in collaboration with the EuroHub platform and the NGO, EasyBusiness, this full-day roundtable brought together 28 CSO and government participants to review screening results and refine recommendations for the National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (NPAA). It provided CSOs with strategic guidance on engagement in negotiation working groups. The EuroHub platform remained central to coordinating CSO alignment with Ukraines EU integration efforts. It hosted joint dialogues on screening feedback, shadow reporting by CSOs, and coordination with government stakeholders. Through this mechanism, CSOs gained visibility into official processes and developed coherent, cross-sector advocacy positions.
4. Annual Partner Meeting in Hlibivka After nearly four years of disruption due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the outbreak of full-scale war, the Annual Sida CSO Partner Meeting was finally held in person on 34 October 2024 in Hlibivka. This marked the first physical gathering of all Sida-supported CSOs since early 2020 and held deep symbolic and emotional significance for all participants. For many CSO representatives, this event was not only a rare opportunity to reconnect in person but a powerful reminder of solidarity, shared purpose, and resilience under extraordinary circumstances. The war had not only strained institutional capacities but also taken a heavy psychological toll on CSO leaders and staff. Coming together, exchanging experiences face-to-face, and finding encouragement in each others stories offered a moment of emotional relief, collective strength, and reaffirmation of mission.
Strategically, the meeting focused both on Sidas Ukraine Strategy and second on the shifting role of CSOs in Ukraines EU accession negotiations, providing a platform for dialogue, knowledge-sharing, and coordination. Sessions explored challenges in legislative screening, wartime communications, and CSOgovernment cooperation mechanisms. The presence of senior Sida representatives from Stockholm and the Swedish Embassy in Kyiv further underscored the importance Sweden places on civil society as a driver of democratic reform and European integration. Their attendance was not only appreciated on a political level but deeply valued as a gesture of trust and long-term partnership during one of the most testing periods in Ukraines modern history. The meeting, also attended by a representative from the EU Delegation in Ukraine, reaffirmed that CSOs are not just recipients of aid or observers of reform - but vital, proactive contributors to Ukraines reconstruction and democratic future.
5. CSO-Government dialogue and cooperation on EU Integration Within Swedens strategy for Ukraine, reform and reconstruction are not separate aims but mutually reinforcing pillars - both serving the overarching objective of supporting Ukraines path to EU membership. In the lead-up to the EuroHub roundtable on 20 December 2024, NCG together with EasyBusiness coordinated a structured behind-the-scenes consultation process to ensure that CSO partners could meaningfully contribute to the Ukrainian Governments development of the National Programme for the Adoption of the Acquis (NPAA). Beginning in October 2024, NCG conducted a series of bilateral consultations and small-group meetings with Sida-supported CSOs, and other key actors engaged in EU-related reforms. These discussions helped identify which chapters of the EU acquis each CSO was actively monitoring, uncovered gaps and risks in the Governments early NPAA drafting process and surfaced cross-cutting priorities including anti-corruption safeguards, judicial independence, human rights protections, and transparency measures. Special efforts were made to include regional CSOs and those working in sensitive sectors such as transitional justice, LGBTQ rights, education, and psycho-social support.
Drawing on this input aligned with Swedens overarching strategic objective of supporting Ukraines path to EU membership and with approval from the Swedish Embassy in Kyiv - NCG supported several CSOs - including TIU, CEDEM, ALI, and IRF - in drafting targeted policy recommendations for specific EU negotiation chapters, particularly Clusters 1 and 2. These thematic inputs were compiled and synthesised by NCG and EasyBusiness and discreetly shared with relevant government bodies in advance of the roundtable, including the Government Office for Coordination of European and Euro-Atlantic Integration and the Ministry of Justice. To enhance coherence, the draft CSO recommendations were then subjected to a peer review process through the EuroHub platform. This step allowed for cross-validation, harmonisation of terminology, and alignment of advocacy positions - especially around procurement, statistics, and judicial reform - while also ensuring that gender and inclusion perspectives were integrated.
A final pre-event coordination session was held during the week prior to the roundtable, where CSOs aligned messaging and reaffirmed guiding principles for engagement: to offer constructive, non-adversarial input; to maintain independence without substituting government roles; and to clearly demonstrate the added value of civil society expertise in the accession process. This thorough preparation enabled CSOs to speak with credibility, clarity, and collective purpose during the December 20 dialogue, resulting in a well-received exchange with senior government officials and the establishment of working groups for continued collaboration on NPAA implementation processes Sida will hopefully continue supporting from 2025 onwards.
*********************************************** 1. What have the operations led to? The operations led to significant institutional strengthening of over 15 Ukrainian civil society organisations (CSOs). The Sida-funded support enabled CSOs to improve governance structures, strategic planning, resilience, and advocacy capabilities. CSOs are now better equipped to contribute to Ukraines EU integration, democratic reform, and post-war recovery.
2. What has changed? •CSOs have enhanced internal governance, with clearer separation of board and executive functions. •There is greater strategic clarity and planning capacity, supported by Results-Based Management and Human Rights-Based Approaches. •Psychological resilience and mental health practices have been integrated into organizational development. •CSOs have become active participants in EU accession processes, notably in legislative screening and policy advocacy. •Coordination mechanisms like EuroHub and Annual Partner Meetings have deepened collaboration and policy coherence.
3. Who has changed what attitude, behaviour or relations in what way? •CSO leaders and staff have adopted more structured and professional management and board practices. •CSOs have shifted from being primarily service providers or watchdogs to becoming collaborative policy actors, especially in EU integration dialogues. •Relationships between CSOs and the Ukrainian government have evolved from distant to cooperative, with formal engagement in policy drafting and legislative review. •There is increased emphasis on inclusive participation, including LGBTQ and regional CSOs, in shaping national reform agendas.
4. What is the target group capable of doing now that they were not capable of doing at the beginning of the intervention? •CSOs are now capable of: oConducting strategic planning using Results Assessment Frameworks. oParticipating meaningfully in EU accession processes, including shadow reporting and policy drafting. oImplementing trauma-informed practices and mental health support for staff. oEngaging in cross-sector advocacy and donor engagement with improved financial governance. oNavigating complex regulatory and political environments with adaptive and resilient operations.
5. Are the operations making a difference? Yes. The operations have made a significant and measurable difference: •CSOs are more resilient, better governed, and strategically aligned with Ukraines reform and EU integration agenda. •They have transitioned from reactive, crisis-mode functioning to proactive, policy-shaping roles. •The intervention helped sustain the civil society ecosystem during war and crisis, while laying the foundation for long-term engagement in national reconstruction.
